space mixing at boundary patches propagates into feature space. Across 26k foreground patches,
feature entropy rises and the top-2 assignment margin falls as patch–boundary overlap increases,

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The reported outcomes are measured against external ground-truth part segmentation and landmark annotations, not against the DINO features or clustering prototypes used to construct the system.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Standard benchmark metrics (NMI, ARI, NME) computed against independent ground-truth part annotations and landmark keypoints across four established datasets.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Training-free K-means clustering over pooled regional features from a frozen DINOv2 backbone, with region generation using RAMP and watershed segmentation.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported performance metrics directly support the claims: Part-DINO outperforms training-free patch-based baselines across all datasets on ARI and NME, while remaining competitive with trained unsupervised and weakly supervised models.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The framework is thoroughly evaluated across four standard benchmarks (CUB, CelebA, PartImageNet-OOD, PartImageNet-Seg) using standard ground-truth metrics (NMI, ARI, NME), alongside granular ablations on region representations, segmentation algorithms, and region merge operations.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Evaluations rely entirely on external ground-truth part segmentation and landmark keypoint annotations across four established benchmarks.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Standard benchmark evaluation metrics (NMI, ARI, and landmark NME) calculated against independent ground-truth annotations.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Training-free K-means clustering on pooled regional features extracted from a frozen DINOv2 backbone.

primary.limitations: The authors transparently discuss the requirement of predefining part granularity K and the sensitivity of structural edge extraction to illumination variations, shadows, or low-contrast textures.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is clearly specified, detailing foreground isolation via SAM, contrast edge extraction via the RAMP transform, watershed region partitioning, and pooling of dense DINO features into region descriptors matched to global K-means prototypes.
primary.quality_rationale: The study offers sound empirical motivation supported by an analysis of 26k foreground patches, a clear and modular training-free design, systematic ablations isolating key components, and convincing gains across multiple standard benchmarks.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper demonstrates that spatial imprecision in DINO-based semantic part discovery stems from pixel mixing across the rigid ViT patch grid, and proposes Part-DINO, a training-free framework that pools frozen DINO features within structurally bounded regions derived from low-level edge detection and watershed segmentation.
